pipeline: PyTorch QAT (tanh-GELU) -> ONNX QDQ (INT8) -> NXP onnx2tflite --qdq-aware-conversion -> INT8 TFLite
summary: QDQ-preserving conversion (Path B). The PyTorch model now uses tanh-approximation GELU so the graph lowers to native TANH (no FlexErf), and the ONNX boundary Quantize/Dequantize nodes are stripped to expose full-integer INT8 I/O. Result is TFLite-Micro deployable with no accuracy loss vs the ONNX.

gelu_swap.change: nn.GELU() -> nn.GELU(approximate='tanh') (3 sites: img_proj, sen_proj, head)
gelu_swap.reason: default GELU exports Erf -> 3 FlexErf (TF Select) ops, unsupported by TFLite-Micro
gelu_swap.validated: check_gelu_swap.py: PyTorch test MAE 20.48 identical before/after the swap
gelu_swap.onnx_op_check: Erf=0, Tanh=3 in both fusion_fp32_qat.onnx and fusion_int8_qat.onnx

fp32_io_tflite.io: FP32 NCHW (validation artifact; 602 KB image input exceeds 512 KB SRAM)

deployability.note: INT8 I/O (147 KB image vs 602 KB FP32) + native TANH-only op set resolve both prior blockers.

comparison_onnx2tf_path_a.note: onnx2tf re-runs its own INT8 calibration and discards the QAT/ORT scales -> catastrophic drift
